bibliography.title: Simulation on the internal structure of three-dimensional proximal tibia under different mechanical environments
bibliography.authors: Fang J, Gong H, Kong L, Zhu D.
bibliography.publication_type: Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; research-article; Journal Article

study.research_problem: The proximal tibia adapts its density distribution to altered joint loading, but most earlier remodeling simulations were two-dimensional and offered limited evidence about three-dimensional valgus-related bone-density patterns.
study.exact_gap: Few three-dimensional proximal-tibia studies had connected an explicit quantitative remodeling law and gait-derived loading to clinically defined medial/lateral BMD regions under both normal and valgus mechanical environments (S002:C05-S002:C06).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Simulate equilibrium BMD in a three-dimensional proximal tibia under normal and 6-degree valgus load distributions, compare selected ROI values with published clinical measurements, and explore whether altered mechanical loading can account for the observed medial-lateral density redistribution (S003:C01).
study.study_design: A right proximal-tibia CT from one healthy-knee geometry was meshed in ANSYS, assigned an initially uniform apparent density, loaded using literature-derived mean stance-phase joint and ligament forces, iteratively remodeled with an SED-per-mass law, and then rerun after shifting joint-contact-force allocation toward the lateral plateau for a hypothetical 6-degree valgus condition.
study.sample_or_model: One 34-year-old male right proximal tibia, 176,708 tetrahedral elements in the principal mesh; external comparison values came from published cohorts of 30 young healthy participants and 22 older painful valgus-osteoarthritis patients rather than matched subjects (S005:C01; S008:C02-S008:C04).
comparators: Normal loading: medial/lateral plateau force split 55%/45%
Hypothetical valgus loading: medial/lateral split 33.5%/66.5% with unchanged resultant force
Simulated ROI ratios versus published healthy and valgus-osteoarthritis clinical ROI measurements
Three mesh sizes for numerical sensitivity
method_spine: Define the remodeling stimulus, density bounds, and density-modulus relationship.
Reconstruct one three-dimensional tibial geometry and specify omitted anatomy.
Apply literature-derived contact, shear, ACL, and MCL loads and iterate density to equilibrium.
Compare normal-model morphology and medial/lateral ROI ratios with external clinical benchmarks.
Alter only the assumed plateau load distribution to model valgus and compare with a separate patient cohort.
Test mesh resolution, then separate pattern agreement from causal and clinical prediction claims.

verification: The authors compare three tetrahedral mesh resolutions; the principal and finer meshes differed by approximately 0.013% in average equivalent stress, 1.45% in strain, and 4.53% in SED, whereas the coarser mesh differed more (S009:C05-S009:C06).
The iterative stopping rule and density bounds are stated, but no time-step, solver, implementation-code, or conservation verification is reported (S004:C01-S004:C02).
calibration: The remodeling constants, density-modulus relation, initial density, and loads are adopted from prior literature rather than calibrated to this CT subject or the external cohorts (S004:C01-S006:C01).
validation: Normal-model medial/lateral BMD ratio (1.19) is compared with a published healthy mean (1.20 plus/minus 0.10), and the valgus-model ROI ratio (0.879) with a published valgus-osteoarthritis range (0.878-0.886) (S008:C02-S008:C04).

This is external face/pattern validation across unmatched populations and selected ROIs, not subject-specific spatial validation, longitudinal prediction, or validation of the valgus-to-osteoarthritis causal pathway.
sensitivity: Mesh-size sensitivity is quantified, but no sensitivity analysis covers load magnitude/distribution, remodeling constants B and k, density-modulus law, initial density, contact area, ligament forces, geometry, age, or sex (S009:C05-S009:C06).
application_prediction: Use for early osteoarthritis diagnosis, periprosthetic stress-shielding prediction, or prosthesis optimization is prospective; none of those applications was tested in this paper (S009:C06-S010:C01).

primary_outcomes: The normal model reproduced a cortical shell, medullary cavity, cancellous region, and higher medial than lateral BMD qualitatively (S008:C01).
Normal ROI1/ROI2 BMD values were 1.23/1.03 g per cubic centimetre, giving a ratio of 1.19 versus 1.20 plus/minus 0.10 in the external healthy cohort (S008:C02-S008:C03).
The valgus model produced ROI3/ROI4 BMD values of 0.908/1.033 and a ratio of 0.879, close to the external painful valgus-OA cohort's reported ratio range of 0.878-0.886 (S008:C03-S008:C04).
The finer mesh changed average stress, strain, and SED by less than 5% relative to the principal mesh, supporting the chosen spatial discretization for those aggregate outputs (S009:C05-S009:C06).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Single-geometry computational prediction with mesh verification and selected-ROI external pattern agreement; no longitudinal, subject-specific, experimental intervention, or clinical predictive validation.

argument_map.central_claim: An SED-driven remodeling model can reproduce selected medial-lateral BMD patterns reported for normal and valgus knees, supporting the plausibility that load redistribution contributes to proximal-tibia density adaptation; it does not establish that valgus loading is the main cause of osteoarthritis or that the model is ready for clinical diagnosis or implant optimization.
data: Predicted equilibrium density morphology and ROI BMD ratios under two assumed force distributions (S008:C01-S008:C04).
Published, unmatched clinical ROI values used for external comparison and three-mesh numerical results (S008:C02-S008:C04; S009:C05-S009:C06).
argument_map.warrant: Agreement between a mechanistic model and independent population-level density patterns increases model plausibility for load-associated remodeling, but causal or predictive claims require alternative explanations, subject matching, parameter uncertainty, and prospective validation.
backing: The model follows established remodeling equations and gait-load literature, and aggregate outputs are relatively stable to one mesh refinement (S004:C01-S005:C03; S009:C05-S009:C06).
argument_map.qualifier: Pattern-level plausibility for one tibial geometry under literature-derived equilibrium loading assumptions.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Normal and valgus predictions reuse one young male geometry and uniform initial density; the 'old valgus' label is an imposed loading scenario, not an older patient's anatomy (S005:C01; S006:C01).
The external cohorts differ in age, symptoms, deformity threshold, and anatomy, and only selected ROI summaries are compared.
Cartilage, menisci, and most soft tissues are not explicitly modeled; their effects are reduced to prescribed forces/contact regions (S005:C01-S005:C03; S009:C04).
The valgus force split, unchanged resultant load, and long-term equilibrium are assumptions rather than measured subject-specific exposure (S006:C01).
OA-related age, cartilage, inflammatory, activity, and disease-history effects are not separated from mechanical loading.

measured: One subject's CT geometry and published clinical cohort ROI BMD summaries; no new longitudinal patient BMD or osteoarthritis outcome was measured in this study (S005:C01; S008:C02-S008:C04).
predicted: All internal density fields, ROI BMD values for the modeled geometry, cortical/trabecular morphology, and the response to the imposed valgus force distribution are numerical predictions (S008:C01-S008:C04).
inferred: Selected-ROI agreement is interpreted as general accuracy of the three-dimensional method (S008:C02; S009:C01).
The load-induced BMD pattern is interpreted as evidence that mechanical environment directly causes bone structural abnormality and may cause osteoarthritis (S009:C02-S010:C01).
The M:L BMD ratio is proposed as a diagnostic criterion and the method as a clinical predictor without diagnostic-accuracy testing (S009:C04-S010:C01).
Apparent age-related cortical/density differences emerge despite using the same young geometry and altered loading, so age interpretation is not independently supported (S009:C02-S009:C03).
recommended: Validate full spatial density distributions in subject-matched normal and valgus cohorts, quantify parameter/load uncertainty, add cartilage/meniscus/contact mechanics, and test prospective prediction before diagnostic or implant-design use.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: A medial/lateral BMD ratio is a bone-distribution proxy, not an osteoarthritis diagnosis or symptom/function endpoint.
Equilibrium remodeling under an assumed force split is not a longitudinal disease trajectory.
Agreement at four ROIs does not validate the complete three-dimensional field.
Mesh convergence of average FE quantities does not validate the remodeling law, biological parameters, boundary conditions, or clinical predictions.
A model suitable for mechanistic exploration is not automatically suitable for patient-level diagnosis or prosthesis optimization.
overclaim_risks: 'Main cause' and 'direct reason' exceed a two-scenario model and unmatched cross-sectional benchmark (S001:C02; S009:C04-S009:C05).
'Accurately predict' is stronger than selected-ROI pattern agreement without out-of-sample subject-level error analysis (S008:C02; S009:C06-S010:C01).
Calling the second simulation 'old people with valgus deformity' obscures that age-specific anatomy/materials were not modeled (S006:C01).
The proposed clinical diagnostic criterion lacks threshold selection, discrimination, calibration, and prospective outcome validation (S010:C01).

section_moves.move: Stage model credibility before the pathological application
section_moves.execution: The paper first simulates a normal condition and compares its ROI ratio with healthy observations, then changes the load distribution for the valgus scenario (S003:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For mechanobiological FE studies, establish a baseline credibility case before the application case and state exactly which inputs change between them.
section_moves.failure_mode: A plausible baseline does not validate every altered-load scenario or causal interpretation.

section_moves.move: Pair model predictions with an external benchmark at matched anatomical regions
section_moves.execution: Simulated and clinical medial/lateral ROIs are defined with comparable landmarks and reported side by side (S007:C01-S008:C04).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Report predicted value, measured comparator, population, anatomical locator, unit, and discrepancy together; then name all mismatches in geometry and cohort.
section_moves.failure_mode: Close ratios from unmatched cohorts are face validation, not proof of patient-level accuracy.

section_moves.move: Quantify mesh sensitivity with decision-relevant outputs
section_moves.execution: Three mesh sizes are compared for average equivalent stress, strain, and SED, with relative differences and computation trade-off (S009:C05-S009:C06).
section_moves.transferable_principle: State mesh size, element count, outputs, relative change, and acceptance rationale; keep mesh verification distinct from biological or clinical validation.
section_moves.failure_mode: Converged discretization does not make uncertain loads or material/remodeling laws correct.

section_moves.move: Separate model-output agreement from causality and application
section_moves.execution: The discussion moves from ROI agreement to causal OA and diagnostic claims without intermediate tests (S009:C01-S010:C01), exposing a reusable audit point.
section_moves.transferable_principle: Write model output, external agreement, mechanistic interpretation, and proposed clinical use as four distinct claim levels, each with its own validation requirement.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not convert pattern agreement into disease causation or diagnostic readiness.

author_reported: The model omits explicit articular cartilage and focuses on bone morphology; cartilage effects are represented indirectly through loading (S009:C04).
reader_identified: One young male geometry represents both normal-young and old-valgus conditions.
No subject-specific or time-resolved load measurement; the valgus split and unchanged resultant force are assumptions.
Uniform initial density and equilibrium remodeling obscure history dependence and disease progression.
Cartilage, menisci, fibula, muscles, and most ligaments are not explicitly modeled; contact and tissue interactions are simplified.
External validation uses unmatched literature cohorts and selected ROI ratios rather than full-field, subject-specific data.
No sensitivity analysis for loads, remodeling constants, density-modulus law, initial density, geometry, age, or sex.
No diagnostic-accuracy, longitudinal OA, intervention, or implant model validates proposed applications.
likely_bias_direction: Selecting ROI ratios close to published values may overstate full-field model accuracy.
Holding geometry and resultant force fixed likely understates physiological variability while making mechanical redistribution appear causally sufficient.
Clinical and causal language overstates an otherwise useful plausibility model.
limitations.scope_boundary: The paper supports a plausible association between imposed medial-lateral load redistribution and predicted equilibrium BMD distribution in one proximal-tibia model. It does not prove valgus-induced osteoarthritis, establish a diagnostic criterion, or validate periprosthetic design predictions.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate numerical verification, parameter sourcing/calibration, external validation, sensitivity, and application prediction in mechanobiological FE manuscripts.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods credibility table, Results, Discussion, and claim audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Mesh convergence and selected-ROI agreement answer different credibility questions and cannot be merged into a generic 'validated model' statement.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write computational evidence as model prediction, external measurement, mechanistic inference, and clinical proposal in distinct layers.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: External pattern agreement does not establish causation, diagnostic discrimination, or prospective prediction.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Audit whether pathology labels correspond to modeled biology or merely to altered boundary conditions imposed on the same geometry.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Model description, comparator fairness, and limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A young geometry with a shifted force split is a hypothetical valgus-loading scenario, not a validated old-OA patient model.

critical_weaknesses: One geometry and assumed loads stand in for age- and disease-specific conditions.
Validation is limited to selected ROI agreement with unmatched cohorts.
Causal and clinical claims exceed the model and uncertainty analysis.

summary_zh: 这篇论文真正提供的是一个三维骨重塑模型的机械可解释性案例：同一胫骨几何在正常与外翻假设载荷下产生不同的内外侧 BMD 分布，选定 ROI 比值与两组既往临床测量接近；它还报告了网格敏感性。写作时必须把这些层级拆开：网格收敛属于数值验证，文献参数不是个体校准，ROI 接近属于外部模式一致性，BMD 场是模型预测，而‘外翻是骨关节炎主要原因’和‘可用于临床诊断’只是更高层推断。尤其要说明所谓老年外翻模型仍使用一名年轻男性的同一几何，仅改变了假定的载荷分配。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section.
The in-vivo-animal cue is false; published clinical values are external benchmarks, not a new cohort in this paper.
The most useful transferable contrast is mesh verification versus model validation versus disease-causality inference.
